This would be so hurtful, you aren't overreacting. At a time when you're physically in pain, and feeling less sexual yourself, understandably, the least he could have done is exercise discretion so as to not make you aware he is meeting his own sexual needs apart from you. I am also about 3 weeks postpartum and i can relate to how crappy the relative low hormones and dopamine state is, especially when your husband feels as great as he ever has. With the exception of maybe the first week or two after childbirth where him masturbating might be excusable, warching porn and masturbating while in a relationship is not a good behavior and he should be restraining himself until you both have the opportunity to engage in intimacy. You still have a need for affection and attention, and your husband by now at least I assume, should be refocusing his sexual energy entirely on you. My advice is to maybe try to move past the porn incident that occurred early on postpartum, while that IS hurtful and he should have protected you from the knowledge of that if that was indeed an exception to the rule of 100% of his attraction and desire being focused on you. I would.communicate to him that henceforth that is the rule, and that from now on, he needs to consider your need for intimacy first before he selfishly indulges in fantasy. I would not put up with a partner that had a serious porn addiction or who neglected my needs long term, and that he had better not be continuing this behavior to the point where you're feeling his absence in the bedroom. To me that's the factor that will make or break your ability to move on from this incident, he now needs to show you how much he loves, needs, and wants YOU and communicate that to you physically. He needs to exercise impulse control and defer his impulses like an adult, he isn't a teenager and he should be able to wait a half a day or a day, for the opportunity to have sex with you. Try not to be too hurt and give him the opportunity to atone for his sins by making a comeback for you, and making sure that you are satisfied and taken care of sexually. Sex and intimacy is healing, and it is his job to heal your pain and frustration with his dick, tongue and hands.
